paper_title: Coupling effect between electromigration and joule heating on the failure of ball grid array in 3D integrated circuit technology
paper_geometry_material: 500 um BGA solder joints, Cu UBM 16 um / 68 um
what_it_establishes: Establishes the accelerated-stress regime for a BGA of comparable size and the existence of ~22x current crowding at the UBM contact. Does NOT establish an allowable: every listed condition is a deliberate failure-inducing stress.
final_status: BOUNDED -- 1.5 A/ball retained as a provisioning rule, NOT an EM-safe limit
our_operating_point: BGA average J = 1178 A/cm2 (Z1) / 1181 (Z2) at 400 um ball, 1.48 A/ball
transferability_caveat: accelerated stress condition; NOT a design allowable

paper_title: Size effect on shear performance of microscale ball grid array structure Cu/Sn-3.0Ag-0.5Cu/Cu solder joints under current stressing
paper_geometry_material: Cu/SAC305/Cu microscale BGA, several joint heights
paper_conditions: 6.0e3 to 1.1e4 A/cm2 under shear + current stressing
what_it_establishes: Shows shear strength and fracture depend on joint height and current crowding. Our geometry and loading differ; informs caution, sets nothing.
our_operating_point: BGA average J = 1178 A/cm2 (Z1) / 1181 (Z2) at 400 um ball, 1.48 A/ball
transferability_caveat: accelerated stress condition; NOT a design allowable

paper_title: Effect of βSn grain orientations on the electromigration-induced evolution of voids in SAC305 BGA solder joints
paper_geometry_material: SAC305 BGA joints, betaSn grain orientation study
what_it_establishes: Grain-orientation dependence means a single scalar EM allowable is not well-defined for SAC305 at joint scale.
our_operating_point: BGA average J = 1178 A/cm2 (Z1) / 1181 (Z2) at 400 um ball, 1.48 A/ball

paper_title: A study on the effects of electrical and thermal stresses on void formation and migration lifetime of Sn3.0Ag0.5Cu solder joints
paper_conditions: electrical and thermal stressing, void formation and migration lifetime
what_it_establishes: Lifetime is a function of combined electrical and thermal stress; supports refusing a current-only allowable.
our_operating_point: BGA average J = 1178 A/cm2 (Z1) / 1181 (Z2) at 400 um ball, 1.48 A/ball

paper_title: Electromigration-induced failure in operando characterization of 3D interconnects: microstructure influence
what_it_establishes: 1 MA/cm2 is an accelerated stress condition used to force failure in observable time. Treating it as a design allowable would be a category error.
final_status: OPEN -- no TSV current-density allowable is asserted
transferability_caveat: accelerated stress condition; NOT a design allowable

paper_title: Role of Cu/SiO<sub>2</sub> Rough Interface in TSV for High-Power Device Under Electromigration
paper_geometry_material: TSV with rough Cu/SiO2 interface, W-M fractal model
what_it_establishes: Current and stress concentrate at interface roughness, so a smooth-via J estimate understates local stress. Supports keeping the allowable OPEN.

paper_title: TSV Electromigration Failure Prediction Using Multiphysics Coupled Energy Method
what_it_establishes: Reliability needs J, T and stress together; a current-density number alone is not a sufficient criterion.

paper_title: Electromigration reliability and morphologies of Cu pillar with microbump under high current density stressing
paper_geometry_material: Cu pillar + Sn microbump, fine pitch
paper_conditions: 3e5 A/cm2 at 150 C; resistance rises abruptly as voids form and solder converts to Cu6Sn5 then Cu3Sn
what_it_establishes: Demonstrates that microbump resistance is NOT constant and NOT zero: it evolves with IMC conversion. Confirms R_contact = 0 is 'not modelled', not 'negligible'. Gives no transferable room-temperature contact resistance for our geometry.
final_status: OPEN -- must become a sourced bracket before any 'non-dominant' claim
transferability_caveat: accelerated stress condition; NOT a design allowable

paper_title: Interfacial Reaction Effect on Electrical Reliability of Cu Pillar/Sn Bumps
paper_geometry_material: Cu pillar / Sn bumps, interfacial reaction
what_it_establishes: Interfacial reaction changes electrical behaviour over time.

paper_title: Study on the Evolution Mechanism of Micro-Bump Contact Resistance in Chiplet Packaging Considering Electro-Thermo-Mechanical Coupling
paper_conditions: contact resistance evolution vs real contact area, softening, stress
what_it_establishes: Directly on point for whether contact resistance belongs in the model. Abstract not retrievable through Crossref or OpenAlex in this environment, so it is recorded as a lead, not as a numerical source.

paper_title: Observation of Intermetallic Compound Formation in Under-Bump Metallization Layers for Scaled Cu/Sn Microbumps
paper_geometry_material: scaled Cu/Sn microbumps, IMC in UBM layers
what_it_establishes: IMC fraction grows as bumps scale, so a bulk-Cu microbump resistance is a lower bound. Abstract not retrievable here.

paper_title: Vertical interconnects of microbumps in 3D integration
paper_geometry_material: review: vertical interconnects of microbumps in 3-D integration
what_it_establishes: Background on UBM, IMC and EM failure modes.

paper_title: Nanotwinning-assisted structurally stable copper for fine-pitch redistribution layer in 2.5D/3D IC packaging
paper_geometry_material: fine-pitch RDL Cu, nanotwinned vs coarse grain
paper_conditions: surface roughening after seed etch; q-time oxidation
what_it_establishes: Establishes that fine-pitch RDL resistance and EM lifetime depend on microstructure, surface roughness and oxidation -- so a bulk-Cu resistivity is a lower bound on RDL resistance, not a nominal value.
final_status: BOUNDED -- bulk Cu rho is a floor; the realized value is higher by an unquantified factor

paper_title: Research on Electromigration Failure Behavior of Redistribution Layer Based on Electrothermal Coupling
paper_conditions: strong temperature-dependent degradation under high-J stressing
what_it_establishes: Supports making R_RDL a function of temperature inside the ET fixed point. Its accelerated J is NOT a design allowable.

paper_title: Electrical Resistance Evolution of Cu Redistribution Layer Electroplated on a Si Interposer
paper_geometry_material: electroplated Cu RDL on Si interposer
what_it_establishes: Electroplated RDL resistance evolves; supports a bounded rather than fixed value.

paper_title: Effect of electroplating current density and post-annealing on the warpage and reliability of redistribution layer for advanced semiconductor package
paper_geometry_material: electroplating current density and post-annealing effects
what_it_establishes: Thermomechanical/process evidence; justifies a bounded RDL material treatment.
